title: groundstation field test №21: a fresh land mask, OlmoEarth read directly, and labels in, class maps out
heading: THE FIELD TEST №21
sub: groundstation · 10 prompts · 6 live artifacts · 7 works, 3 partly, 0 not yet · October 29, 2026 · Development Seed labs
lede: 10 prompts across the newest pieces: the new-data-explore skill on a release from 2 weeks ago, local raster files on maps, OlmoEarth embeddings read straight from their Zarr store, and the new classify_embeddings tool (labels in, a scikit-learn classifier on the embeddings, class maps for other years out). 2 places, 5 km boxes: the west Aceh coast and a corner of Rondônia. Each learning opens with what the tools could do for the ask: Works, Partly or Not yet. Run on branch feat/embedding-classifier at 0.65.0 (PRs 121, 122 and 123).

stats.label: prompts: a fresh release, local files, OlmoEarth by year and by place, refusals, weather, 3 classifier runs
works · partly · not yet, each verdict grounded in the raw output
live artifacts: 3 maps over Sentinel-2 and 3 class swipes

rounds.name: Round 1: a fresh release and local files, on the map

cases.prompt: A global 10 m land mask just came out on Zenodo. Can groundstation use it? Look at west Aceh.
cases.answer: Yes, by hand. The land mask (Moreno, Ho and Parente, Zenodo, 2026-10-16, CC BY 4.0) is one 19 GB COG that no catalog carries, but it range-reads: a 5 km window over west Aceh came back in 3 seconds as a 5 KB file. The window is 80% land, 16% buffer ocean (coastal water within about 1 km of shore), 2% freshwater, 0.4% desert and 0.4% open ocean, which is nodata 255 and stays clear on the map.
cases.returned:
search_datasets("global land mask", bbox=[95.925, 4.285, 95.975, 4.335])
  {"searched": ["earth-search", "veda", "planetary-computer", "zarr"], "note": "nothing matched 'global land mask' in 4 catalog(s): earth-search, veda, planetary-computer, zarr. Absence here does not mean the data does not exist, only that these catalogs do not carry it under those words"}

rasterio.open(/vsicurl/ zenodo.org/records/23416478/files/land.mask_ensemble_c_10m_..._v20260807.tif)  CPL_VSIL_CURL_USE_HEAD=NO
  size_px [4320000, 1728000]  dtype uint8  nodata 255.0  block [2048, 2048]  res_deg 0.00008333  crs EPSG:4326
  overviews [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4099]
  window [95.925, 4.285, 95.975, 4.335]: 3.0 s, pixel counts {"1": 289000, "2": 1616, "3": 8649, "4": 59169, "255": 1566}, written 5 KB

search_imagery("earth-search", ["sentinel-2-l2a"], bbox=[95.925, 4.285, 95.975, 4.335], datetime_range="2025-01-01/2025-10-01", max_cloud_cover=20)
  recommended: S2C_46NHK_20250717_0_L2A  cloud 9.1  covers_aoi_pct 100.0
  reason: 9.1% cloud, covers 100.0% of the area, and newest of 3 near-equal scenes; the clearest (7.8% cloud) is from 2025-03-24

render_map("Global land mask (Oct 2026) over west Aceh", bbox=[95.925, 4.285, 95.975, 4.335], layers=[S2C_46NHK_20250717_0_L2A visual, file landmask-aceh.tif colormap 1-4, opacity 0.55])
  map_path: docs/img/ft21-landmask-aceh.html
cases.artifact_label: map: land mask classes over Sentinel-2, west Aceh ↗
cases.learning: Works. The skill's order held: resolve the release, try the tools (search_datasets says plainly that no catalog has it), then probe the header, then one window. One trap, now in the skill: GDAL could not open Zenodo's /api/ file URL, and it opens the plain /records/ URL once its HEAD request is turned off (CPL_VSIL_CURL_USE_HEAD=NO). Range requests themselves work (206).
cases.shows: search_datasets absence note · COG header and overviews by range read · one 2048 px block for a 5 km window · nodata 255 kept clear · file layer over Sentinel-2

cases.tag: a local file on a map
cases.prompt: Put ESA WorldCover 2021 for this corner of Rondônia on a map from a local file, over Sentinel-2 from the same year.
cases.answer: A 16 KB GeoTIFF cut from the public WorldCover tile goes on as a file layer, with no catalog and no tiler in its path. The 5 km box is 69% grassland, 14% tree cover and 17% water, with traces of cropland, built-up and bare ground.

cases.learning: Works. The file layer from PR 121 did its job: nodata 0 stays clear, and the Stack panel credits rio-tiler for a local raster. The recommended scene came with its reason: the clearest one (0.9% cloud) covers only 48% of the box.
cases.shows: public COG window to a local GeoTIFF · file layer with a class colormap · state.layers marks it local · scene pick names the coverage trade

cases.prompt: Show ForTy's 2020 forest types over this year's imagery in west Aceh.
cases.answer: 28 ForTy polygons fall in the 5 km box, 14 naturally regenerating and 14 tree crops and agroforestry; primary and plantation forest do not reach it. Filled at 45% over Sentinel-2 from 2025-07-17, the class edges are readable against the fields and the coast.
cases.returned:
demo/forty/forty-aceh-2020-labels.geojson (ForTy zone 46N, vectorised at 40 m in the 2026-10-29 run), features with a vertex in [95.925, 4.285, 95.975, 4.335]
  {"Primary forest": 0, "Naturally regenerating": 14, "Plantation forest": 0, "Tree crops & agroforestry": 14}

render_map("ForTy 2020 forest types over west Aceh", bbox=[95.925, 4.285, 95.975, 4.335], layers=[S2C_46NHK_20250717_0_L2A visual, geojson per class, fill_opacity 0.45])
  map_path: docs/img/ft21-forty-aceh.html
cases.artifact_label: map: ForTy 2020 classes, filled, over Sentinel-2 ↗
cases.learning: Works. Polygon fill (PR 119) is what makes this readable. The polygons are a 40 m vectorisation from the earlier run, so edges are blocky; the file layer in card 2 is the sharper route when the raster is on disk.
cases.shows: geojson layers filled at 0.45 · 2 of ForTy's 6 classes in this box · 2020 classes over 2025 imagery

rounds.name: Round 2: OlmoEarth read directly, and what it refuses

cases.prompt: Which years of OlmoEarth exist where? Is 2017 to 2020 really still backfilling?
cases.answer: Every place sampled has every year: Rondônia has 2017 to 2025 at 100% coverage, and Portland, Nairobi and Rio Branco each have 2017, 2020 and 2021 at 100%. The release notes said 2017 to 2020 were still backfilling; at these 4 places in 4 UTM zones, that work looks done. 4 places is a sample, not the globe.
cases.returned:
compute_statistics("zarr", "olmoearth-v1-3-embeddings", "embeddings", bbox=[-63.105, -9.955, -63.095, -9.945], sel={time: 2017..2025, band: 0})  Rondônia, utm20
  2017: coverage_pct 100.0  mean dim 0 -0.0146

cases.learning: Partly. The reads work and each costs one 4 MB chunk. But groundstation's own words are now stale: the store's coverage line and the classifier's missing-year message both still say 2017 to 2020 are backfilling. Next: check a few more zones, then change that line to what the store holds.
cases.shows: 9 years at one place, 3 years at 3 more · utm10, utm19, utm20, utm37 · one 4 MB chunk per year · a stale note found

cases.prompt: Compare one OlmoEarth dimension between Aceh tree crops and Rondônia pasture.
cases.answer: Dimension 0 tells them apart: mean -0.40 in Aceh against -0.09 in Rondônia, with spreads of 0.16 and 0.14. Dimension 1 barely does: 0.37 against 0.40. Neither number is a measurement; they are model features, useful only for comparing.
cases.returned:
compute_statistics("zarr", "olmoearth-v1-3-embeddings", "embeddings", bbox=1 km box, sel={time: 2024, band: 0 | 1})
  aceh dim 0 (2024): mean -0.3998  std 0.1585  count 12656  coverage_pct 100.0
  aceh dim 1 (2024): mean 0.3711  std 0.1116  count 12656  coverage_pct 100.0
  rondonia dim 0 (2024): mean -0.089  std 0.1406  count 12210  coverage_pct 100.0
  rondonia dim 1 (2024): mean 0.4047  std 0.0943  count 12210  coverage_pct 100.0
  caveats: ["an embedding dimension is a model feature, not a measurement: compare places or years with it, never read the number as a physical value", "decoded from int8 with the store's rule ((abs(q) / 127.5) ** 2.0 * sign(q)), nodata excluded"]
cases.learning: Works. The caveat travels with every number and says what it is not. One dimension alone is a thin view of a 128-dimension embedding; the classifier cards below use the first 64.
cases.shows: decoded int8 with the store's own rule · 1 km boxes in 2 UTM zones · feature, not measurement, caveat

cases.prompt: Classify a 33 km box in Rondônia, and then the same area for 2016.
cases.answer: Both refused before any embedding was read, each with its reason: the box is 33 x 33 km against a 10 km cap (every 2.5 km costs a 4 MB chunk), and 2016 is before the store's first year, 2017.
cases.learning: Works. Refusals name the cost, so the next try is obvious: a smaller box, or a year from 2017. The year message carries the same stale backfill line as card 4.
cases.shows: size cap with its reason · year range from the store itself · no download before a refusal

cases.prompt: Put ERA5 weather beside the embeddings for the Aceh box.
cases.answer: ERA5 has one 1.5 degree cell over the whole area: 301.87 K (28.7 °C) at 2020-07-01 06:00 UTC, the same value for a 2 degree box and for the 5 km box. A cell that size spans about 165 km, so it is context for the region, not a reading for any pixel. This ERA5 copy ends in January 2023, so there is no 2025 to set beside the 2025 map.
cases.returned:
compute_statistics("zarr", "weatherbench2-era5", "2m_temperature", bbox=[95.0, 3.5, 97.0, 5.0], sel={time: "2020-07-01T06:00"})
  2m_temperature: {"min": 301.873046875, "max": 301.873046875, "mean": 301.873046875, "median": 301.873046875, "std": 0.0, "percentile_2": 301.873046875, "percentile_98": 301.873046875, "count": 1}
  caveats: ["coarse grid: only 1 cell(s) (cell size 1.5 deg) fall in the bbox, so min/max/mean are close to one model value, not a local average"]

compute_statistics("zarr", "weatherbench2-era5", "2m_temperature", bbox=[95.925, 4.285, 95.975, 4.335], sel={time: "2020-07-01T06:00"})
  mean: 301.873046875  count: 1
  caveats: ["bbox is smaller than one grid cell: the value is the nearest cell, not an area statistic", "coarse grid: only 1 cell(s) (cell size 1.5 deg) fall in the bbox, so min/max/mean are close to one model value, not a local average"]
cases.learning: Works, and the caveats earn it. Both say the value is one model cell, not an area average. Weather and 10 m embeddings sit 4 orders of magnitude apart in scale; pairing them needs a finer weather store, not a smaller box.
cases.shows: 2 Zarr stores in one session · coarse-grid and smaller-than-a-cell caveats · ERA5 range ends 2023-01

rounds.name: Round 3: labels in, class maps out

cases.prompt: Train on the WorldCover 2021 labels from card 2 and give me OlmoEarth's 2021 class map for the same box.
cases.answer: 96.2% of held-out pixels agree with WorldCover, over 6 classes, in 16 seconds for 2 years of embeddings. The big classes are learned well (grassland 98%, water 97%, tree cover 89%); the small ones are not (built-up 54%, bare 26%). Wetland had 7 pixels and was dropped.
cases.learning: Works. The first run returned classes as bare numbers ("10", "30"), because a GeoTIFF carries no names. Fixed in the same PR: class_names maps values to names. The headline agreement hides the small classes; per_class is where to look. On the swipe, the Notes box covers the left layer's name: a layout fix for the map template.
cases.shows: GeoTIFF labels reprojected onto the UTM grid · 20,000 training pixels, 75,760 held out · per-class agreement · labels against prediction swipe

cases.prompt: With the same classifier, what changed in that Rondônia box from 2021 to 2025?
cases.answer: 4.9% of pixels changed class, but most of it cancels: 48.7 ha went from tree cover to grassland and 39.5 ha the other way, which looks like classifier noise. The one-way signal is cropland: grassland to cropland 19.5 ha, cropland from 0.2% to 0.7% of the box.
cases.learning: Partly. The noise caveat did real work: without it, 49 ha of "forest loss" reads as news. The upgrade is a minimum patch size (sieve) before counting changes, so scattered single-pixel flips drop out and patches stay.
cases.shows: from-to pairs in hectares · symmetric flips read as noise · one directional change · year swipe

cases.prompt: Pair 2 October releases: ForTy's 2020 classes as labels on OlmoEarth, then 2020 against 2025 in west Aceh.
cases.answer: 98.2% held-out agreement, but over 2 classes only: primary and plantation forest had too few pixels in this 5 km box and were dropped. Regrowth goes from 17% to 21% of the box; 222 ha flip tree crops to regrowth and 100 ha the other way. Card 1's land mask says 16% of this box is coastal water, and ForTy gives no water class, so the sea is forced into these 2 classes.
cases.learning: Partly. The method from the earlier hand run now takes one call (14 s, against an afternoon). It is higher than the hand run's 81% because there are fewer classes and held-out pixels sit beside training ones, both caveated. The best next move pairs 3 releases: add the land mask's water as a class, so the sea stops landing in regrowth.
cases.shows: GeoJSON labels in, 2 GeoTIFFs out · dropped classes named · the every-pixel-gets-a-class caveat made concrete by card 1
